item.title: Nation's CO2 emissions set to decline as clean energy lead grows
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Nation's CO2 emissions set to decline as clean energy lead grows Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels in China are projected to fall 0.9 percent in 2026 after two years of slow growth, as the country continues to expand the use of renewable energy and electric vehicles, said the 2026 Global Carbon Budget, which was unveiled on Tuesday. The projection comes as climate experts and officials at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, or COP31, highlight China's central role in accelerating the global clean energy transition. The annual UN climate summit, which opened on Monday in Antalya, Turkiye, will run through Nov 20. According to the 2026 Global Carbon Budget, China produces 32 percent of the world's fossil emissions, but it is also the country most active in deploying clean technologies and increasing carbon sinks through reforestation. The country has achieved the largest carbon uptake through its reforestation and afforestation initiatives. In addition, China accounts for half of the emissions avoided worldwide through the use of renewable energy and EVs. Along with a sharp decrease in oil emissions, China's coal emissions are projected to rise by just 0.3 percent, while electricity generation from renewables continues to grow strongly. Globally, CO2 emissions from fossil fuels are projected to fall 0.4 percent to 38.2 billion metric tons this year. While energy demand continues to rise, two-thirds of the increase is being met by greater use of solar and wind power and EVs. However, clean energy growth is still not fast enough to bring about a sustained decline in global CO2 emissions from fossil fuels. An analysis published in the academic journal Nature Climate Change, alongside the report, found that emissions avoided through solar and wind power rose from 0.28 billion tons in 2010 to 4.1 billion tons in 2025, and are projected to reach 4.6 billion tons in 2026. Corinne Le Quere, a Royal Society research professor of climate change science at the University of East Anglia in the United Kingdom, said that clean technologies are making a real difference in reducing global emissions. "Solar and wind power and EVs are expanding rapidly, led by China. Countries on every continent are decreasing their emissions while growing their economies. A further acceleration could turn the tide on global emissions within a few years," she said. Global emissions from oil are projected to decrease 1.9 percent, likely as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the conflict in Iran, according to the report. "A decline in fossil CO2 emissions is encouraging, but a reduction driven partly by geopolitical shocks is not a sustainable climate solution," said Pierre Friedlingstein, director of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University of Exeter in the UK, who led the study. "The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies. While renewables and EVs are increasingly offsetting growth in energy demand, further acceleration is needed if global emissions are to peak and enter a sustained decline," he said. Chris Bowen, COP31 president of negotiations, also highlighted China's contribution to the global energy transition at a side event at the China Pavilion on "Ecological Civilization and Beautiful China Practices" on Tuesday. Bowen, who is also Australia's minister for climate change and energy, said that global renewable energy capacity was expected to grow by 4,800 gigawatts between 2025 and 2030, exceeding the combined power-generation capacity of China, Japan and the European Union. "This is a remarkable achievement, and China is playing a key role in making it possible," he said. "What every country does matters," Bowen said. "Every country matters. But no country matters more than China, not only because of its size and influence, but also because of the impact its investments are having around the world. "China's investments are bringing down the cost of renewable energy for everyone. They are driving down the costs of batteries and solar power. That benefits China's own economic development, but it benefits the rest of the world as well." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Carrying forward "Kuliang friendship" for closer China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Carrying forward "Kuliang friendship" for closer China-U.S. ties Young people from the U.S. visit smart cultivation facilities for specialty fruits at an agricultural science and technology industrial park in Jinhua, east China's Zhejiang province, Oct. 21, 2026. (Photo/Shi Bufa) The 2026 Kuliang Forum was recently held in Fuzhou, southeast China's Fujian province. Friends from all walks of life in China and the U.S. gathered in the city, where the story of Kuliang took place, to relive their transoceanic friendship, discuss shared expectations for people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and rally public support to translate the vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into action. Kuliang, or "Guling" in Mandarin, was once a hillside resort among foreign expatriates in the suburbs of Fuzhou. The story of Kuliang is a well-known example of China-U.S. friendship personally promoted by Chinese President Xi Jinping. It bears the deep and lasting bonds between the Chinese and American people spanning over a century. In 1992, as Fuzhou's Party Secretary, President Xi came across a touching story about Kuliang published in People's Daily. Learning of American professor Milton Gardner's lifelong attachment to Kuliang and his unfulfilled regret of never being able to return, he personally arranged for Mrs. Elizabeth Gardner to visit China and fulfill her late husband's long-cherished wish. In 2023 and 2024, President Xi sent congratulatory letters twice to the "Bond with Kuliang" series of events, encouraging people in both countries to carry forward the Kuliang story and friendship. Young people from the U.S. visit the Grand Canal Banzha Heritage Park in Huai'an, east China's Jiangsu province, July 10, 2026. (Photo/Zhao Qirui) With President Xi's personal attention and support, the Kuliang story continues to take on new vitality. From the heartfelt reunions among the "Friends of Kuliang," a group of descendants of the American families who once lived in Fuzhou, to the screening of the documentary "Dear Kuliang," the Kuliang friendship has become a vivid testament to the lasting, cross-generational bond shared by the Chinese and American peoples. The stories of old friends grow ever richer with the passing of time, while new chapters are continuously written by new friends, helping create a new future for people-to-people friendship between China and the U.S. Before the 2026 Kuliang Forum opened, Chinese and American friends visited Guling together, carrying forward their bond through shared memories and enhancing mutual understanding through face-to-face dialogue. William Brown, an American professor at Xiamen University, returned to Guling after more than 30 years. He said, "Once you truly set foot on this land and get to know its people, estrangement and prejudice melt away. We can become friends and even family." Dante Muñoz, an American vlogger visiting Guling for the first time, used his camera to capture the nature beauty of the misty mountains, saying many truths cannot be fully explained by the internet and books alone and one has to experience them firsthand. Such mutual flow of goodwill between the Chinese and American peoples constantly gathers force to break through barriers and silence discordant noise, quietly anchoring bilateral ties to stay on the right course through thick and thin. Youth are the witnesses and beneficiaries of China-U.S. relations, as well as their future and hope. This year, a growing number of American youth have stepped onto Chinese land to write more Kuliang stories in the new era together with their Chinese counterparts. For instance, the One Voice Children's Choir of the U.S. visited China and sang "We Are Together" for their Chinese friends. Through "pickleball diplomacy," successive batches of young students have built bridges of friendship. While in China, they enjoyed an immersive travel experience, discovered its broader appeal in new ways, and shopped for quality Chinese goods. By bringing a genuine picture of China back home, they serve as a vital stream nourishing U.S.-China relations. After reaching the five-year goal of inviting 50,000 young Americans to China for study and exchanges two and a half years ahead of schedule, President Xi has issued a new call to invite 100,000 more over the coming five years. Scaling up this target and expanding youth exchanges will inject vibrant youth momentum into China-U.S. friendship, passing the torch of friendship from generation to generation. This year marks a major year for China-U.S. relations. Guided by head-of-state diplomacy, bilateral ties have maintained overall stability, and the desire of both peoples to understand and draw closer to one another has grown increasingly strong. Recent polls have shown a gradual improvement in American public perceptions of China, with growing calls for engagement and cooperation. It is hoped that the U.S. side will listen to the public call and respond to the shared desire of both peoples for closer engagement, facilitate deeper cultural and people-to-people exchanges, translate the important consensus reached at high-level dialogues between China and the U.S. into practical actions of cooperation, and turn the rising wave of popular goodwill into a powerful force driving bilateral friendship. As China and the U.S. will respectively host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and the Group of Twenty (G20) Summit, new opportunities will be created for both nations to further deepen exchange and cooperation. By strengthening bonds through cooperation and carefully nurturing the tree of friendship between the Chinese and American peoples, China and the U.S. will help their friendship take deep root, flourish across generations, and remain evergreen through every season, just like the thousand-year-old cedars of Kuliang. item.title: China's Yangtze River Delta forges new quality productive forces through coordinated development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
China's Yangtze River Delta forges new quality productive forces through coordinated development SHANGHAI, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- In east China's Yangtze River Delta, a four-hour drive can take manufacturers through a network of suppliers capable of providing every component needed to build a new-energy vehicle. At one factory, a six-axis industrial robot can be produced every 12 minutes. These examples reflect a broad shift as the region turns its tightly clustered research and innovation hubs into advanced industrial capacity, making what China calls new quality productive forces the main engine of its growth. The Yangtze River Delta, comprising Shanghai and the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, now accounts for about one-quarter of China's GDP and nearly one-third of national R&D spending. According to a recent national assessment of regional science and technology innovation, Shanghai ranked first in comprehensive sci-tech innovation nationwide, with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui also among the top performers. INNOVATION CLUSTERS This transformation is particularly visible in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City, where advanced industries are increasingly concentrated. At a lab in the Shanghai R&D center of XtalPi, an AI drug discovery company listed in Hong Kong, human researchers are largely absent. Weighing powders, controlling temperature during mixing, sampling, filtering and running post-processing analyzes are all handled by robotic workstations directed by AI, with large volumes of experimental data flowing continuously to back-end systems. "Zhangjiang offers a unique advantage in clustering innovation resources," said Wang Mingtai, XtalPi's senior vice president. "From overseas partners and major research institutes to upstream and downstream suppliers, connections can be established quickly here." By June 2026, the company had established partnerships with 17 of the world's top 20 pharmaceutical companies. Since the beginning of the year, more than six innovative drug programs involving its discovery technology had reported positive progress in clinical trials. Its autonomous research platform is also being applied in chemicals, new materials and new energy, alongside collaborations with leading universities and research institutes. The expanding network illustrates how Zhangjiang is bringing together scientific research, industrial partners and the development of new medicines and technologies, helping to move discoveries beyond the laboratory. Over the past five years, industrial output from firms above designated size in Zhangjiang has totaled 1.75 trillion yuan (about 260 billion U.S. dollars). In the first half of 2026, its three priority sectors -- integrated circuits, biomedicine and AI -- generated 82.28 billion yuan in output, up 14.8 percent from a year earlier. The area is now home to eight major global chip companies, 35 registered AI large models, and one in ten innovative drugs developed in China. Zhangjiang's experience shows how a concentration of research institutions, technology companies and industrial resources can accelerate innovation, driving new quality productive forces. The same approach is taking shape across the wider Yangtze River Delta, with its four provincial-level divisions complementing one another, especially in AI and the digital economy. COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS A recent digital development report describes this regional division of labor in simple terms: with Shanghai strengthening foundational research, Jiangsu focusing on manufacturing, Zhejiang excelling in application scenarios, and Anhui aggregating computing power. It allows companies to combine capabilities across the region and form a networked innovation system, rather than replicate them in one place. Jiangsu has made "AI Plus" a central driver of manufacturing upgrading. Under its action plan, the penetration rate of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents is expected to exceed 70 percent by 2027, with the AI industry surpassing 1 trillion yuan by 2030. In Suzhou, for example, efforts are underway to develop 150 industrial vertical large models, along with more than 200 high-quality industrial datasets, pushing AI applications from quality control and maintenance deeper into R&D and design. Zhejiang, meanwhile, is encouraging businesses to develop practical applications for AI, activating its intelligent economy. In 2025, the province's core AI industry revenue exceeded 710 billion yuan, growing by more than 20 percent. The capital city, Hangzhou, is positioning itself as a leading "AI city," deploying multimodal large models and embodied intelligence, while a major open-source model community and five 10,000-GPU computing clusters aim to lower the cost for small and medium-sized enterprises to adopt AI. Anhui is focusing on expanding its digital infrastructure and putting it to wider use. The province plans to build 14,000 new 5G base stations and 4,000 5G-A base stations in 2026, with intelligent computing capacity exceeding 65,000 petaflops. A special fund for data-element reform in the province will support AI scenario projects with up to 10 million yuan each, accelerating deployment in manufacturing, public services and healthcare. CROSS-REGIONAL LINKS Cooperation across the Yangtze River Delta extends beyond AI and the digital economy. It also shows how innovation capacity generated in one city can be rapidly converted into industrial output in another. Suzhou, for example, has 50 enterprises in the supply chain for China's C919 passenger aircraft assembled in Shanghai, and about 180 auto-parts manufacturers have become tier-one suppliers for Shanghai-based SAIC Volkswagen and Tesla. Meanwhile, scientific instruments at Shanghai's universities and research institutes can be booked online by Suzhou enterprises for remote testing and cross-regional settlement. As of October 2026, the Yangtze River Delta region had shared 75,000 sets of large-scale scientific instruments, with sci-tech innovation vouchers covering about 820 million yuan in services. These links make integration tangible: firms can access specialized suppliers and costly scientific equipment across administrative boundaries, lowering duplication and making better use of existing resources. Luo Dajin, director of the Shanghai municipal science and technology commission, said Shanghai would build on its strengths as an international economic, financial, trade, shipping and sci-tech innovation hub, and work with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui to build a sci-tech innovation corridor and other joint innovation zones across the region. Recent data suggest the shift is gaining momentum. In the first three quarters of 2026, high-tech manufacturing output grew 15.1 percent in Jiangsu, 16 percent in Zhejiang and 50.3 percent in Anhui, while Shanghai's three priority industries expanded by 17.1 percent. The region's division of labor has moved beyond the old linear pattern of industrial relocation from Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang to Anhui, and is now shaped by functional and structural complementarity, said Zeng Gang, director of the Institute of Urban Development, East China Normal University. "New quality productive forces have become the main engine of industrial growth in the Yangtze River Delta," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday held positive and constructive phone talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on China-U.S. relations and the interaction between the two heads of state. During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that President Xi Jinping's visit to the United States in September was smooth and successful. The two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-U.S. relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a right approach for the two countries to get along with each other, Wang said. The stable momentum of China-U.S. relations has not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on their respective and common interests, Wang said. China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the U.S. side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results, Wang said. item.title: Chinese VP attends COP31 Antalya Leaders' Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese VP attends COP31 Antalya Leaders' Summit ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, as President Xi Jinping's special representative, attended the Antalya Leaders' Summit of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) on Wednesday and delivered a national statement. Han said that Xi has pointed out that responding to climate change is the common cause of all humanity, adding that the adverse effects of global climate change are becoming increasingly apparent. In light of the new circumstances, Han put forward a four-point proposal. The first is to stay focused on common goals and strengthen collective action. He called for the full and effective implementation of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement in accordance with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, so as to rally collective efforts in global climate governance. Developed countries should take the lead in reducing emissions and fulfill their climate finance commitments, Han said, stressing that all parties should make every effort to implement their nationally determined contributions and strive to do better. The second is to accelerate the green transition and promote low-carbon development. Efforts should be made to facilitate the free flow of high-quality green technologies and products, and promote the transformation and upgrading of the economic and industrial structures, Han said. Noting that China has set targets for 2030, including raising the share of non-fossil energy in total electricity generation to 50 percent and increasing the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35 percent, Han said that China remains firmly committed to achieving its carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals. The third is to prevent climate-related disasters and enhance climate resilience. Equal importance should be attached to mitigation and adaptation, he said, adding that cooperation should be strengthened in areas such as disaster prevention and mitigation, monitoring and early warning, and disaster relief, so as to enhance climate adaptation capacity. He noted that China is willing to promote the application of its intelligent meteorological early warning solution "MAZU" in more countries, helping them prevent and respond to climate risks. The fourth is to adhere to openness and inclusiveness and deepen international cooperation. He said that support and assistance to developing countries should be strengthened to jointly build a clean and beautiful world. China has continued to promote South-South cooperation projects on climate change, such as the "Africa Solar Belt," and will launch the capacity-building project "Global South climate action leadership program," said the Chinese vice president, noting that China will also contribute to the fair and effective implementation of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. item.title: Beyond China's shopping festival: How Singles' Day shifts from local to global retail barometer
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Beyond China's shopping festival: How Singles' Day shifts from local to global retail barometer A drone photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows an intelligent package sorting line in Xinghua City, east China's Jiangsu Province. (Photo by Zhou Shegen/Xinhua) BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Nearly two decades after its launch, China's Singles' Day shopping festival has become an increasingly influential event in global retail. Overseas brands and e-commerce platforms are adjusting their promotional schedules, supply chains and product launches to tap into the Chinese market. Also known as Double 11 because it falls on Nov. 11, the annual online shopping carnival is one of the world's largest retail events. This year's edition, which has run for nearly a month, is set to conclude, highlighting a shift toward a wider range of services, smarter AI shopping assistants and more vibrant two-way trade through cross-border commerce. SERVICE CONSUMPTION AS A NEW ENGINE During this year's event, major e-commerce platforms expanded their offerings beyond traditional consumer goods and discounts, giving greater prominence to services. JD.com showcased more than 100 service products for the first time, while Suning offered packages such as a 9.9-yuan (about 1.47 U.S. dollars) whole-house appliance inspection. The trend reflects broader changes in China's consumer market, which is now driven by both goods and services. In the first three quarters of this year, service retail sales grew 4 percentage points faster than goods retail sales, making services a key source of incremental consumption. A Beijing resident surnamed Feng said his Double 11 purchases included a two-day hotel package and a home cleaning card. "There are more and more services to choose from. Buying these packages on major platforms offers good value, and fulfillment and after-sales service are more reliable," he said. Physical goods, however, remain a major part of the shopping festival. Sales of smartphones covered by government trade-in subsidies on Tmall surged more than ninefold, while transactions in categories such as maternal and infant products and home appliances on Taobao's on-demand retail platform grew more than 70 percent year on year. Combined sales on China's major integrated e-commerce platforms during the early phase of this year's Singles' Day reached 1.0263 trillion yuan as of Oct. 31, data firm Syntun showed. This year, the Tmall Double 11 event featured 1 million global brands and 72 million products in promotion. That contrasts sharply with the first edition in 2009, when only 27 brands took part and transactions totaled 52 million yuan. AI ELEMENTS One notable development this year was the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) tokens as an independent product category on multiple e-commerce platforms, a sign that AI is rapidly integrating into every link of the e-commerce chain. Taobao, Douyin and Pinduoduo all embedded smarter AI shopping functions during this year's Double 11. Last year, Taobao and JD.com introduced AI shopping guides that could answer product questions and search by photo. This year, many platforms rolled out conversational AI shopping assistants for the first time -- tools that can sort shopping carts, automatically calculate combined discounts and subsidies, and handle after-sales follow-up. Li Mingtao, chief e-commerce expert at the China International Electronic Commerce Center, said consumers' use of AI shopping assistants has moved from trial to large-scale adoption, and the expanding functions mark a shift from tools to intelligent agents. "In previous years, consumers spent considerable time hunting for coupons and comparing prices. AI shopping assistants take on that time burden, turning complex promotional rules into clear, actionable shopping plans," Li said. AI is also changing how online retailers operate, improving efficiency and streamlining operations. Alibaba's QwenWork launched an e-commerce version ahead of Singles' Day, while JD.com upgraded its AI business center to provide merchants with dozens of tools covering product selection, operations, fulfillment and after-sales. GLOBAL RESONANCE The festival's influence is increasingly extending beyond China. With the rise of global digital consumption and improving cross-border e-commerce policies, many platforms and merchants looked overseas for new growth during this year's event, while international brands are leveraging China's Singles' Day to expand market share. This year, Taobao opened a one-click overseas channel for the first time, allowing merchants to sell in both domestic and overseas markets with their existing stores and products. AliExpress's official warehouses covered six countries, with pre-event overseas warehouse inventory up 146 percent year on year. "Going overseas is not simply about selling goods abroad," said Sun Yanyan, head of Sparkone Media, a cross-border e-commerce company. "It is about exporting China's mature digital retail, supply chain and AI operations capabilities, building a two-way channel that helps transform Chinese manufacturing into Chinese brands and better connects domestic and international markets." While platforms expand overseas, quality imported goods continue to enrich choices for Chinese consumers. A Shanghai resident surnamed Liu bought Australian infant food and Belgian nutritional supplements on Tmall Global during Singles' Day. "In the past, many overseas local brands were hard to buy," she said. "Now the platform has sufficient bonded warehouse stock and fast customs clearance and delivery, so I can shop for specialty goods from around the world without traveling abroad." Currently, imported food products on the Taobao and Tmall platforms cover more than 100 countries, over 1,000 production regions, and more than one million items. This year, the Singles' Day festival coincided with the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10. The expo attracted 4,142 overseas companies from 162 countries, regions and international organizations, with more than 480 representative new products making their debuts. Many of these products were not merely on display -- they were simultaneously listed on Singles' Day platforms, shortening the distance between global innovation and Chinese consumers. At the Tmall Global booth, AI-related gadgets were among the highlights: Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, Oura smart rings and Fitbit Air wristbands were launched simultaneously at the CIIE and on Singles' Day. According to Tmall Global, more than 1,800 new brands opened stores on the platform over the past year, and 1,300-plus imported brands participated in Singles' Day for the first time. To address information gaps in cross-border shopping, Tmall Global launched a "Global Traceability Program" in May this year. More than 50 global brands have joined, and more than half of participating brands recorded double-digit year-on-year sales growth during this year's Singles' Day. Besides Taobao and Tmall, other Chinese platforms such as Temu, Shein and TikTok Shop have brought Double 11 promotions to dozens of countries, while some Western retailers have adjusted their year-end promotional calendars in response. Eighteen years on, Singles' Day no longer belongs to one country or one platform. From promotional calendars and logistics to product categories and consumer trust, it has become a global retail landmark -- and for many, an increasingly important indicator of changes in China's consumer market and of how the country continues to innovate and open up. item.title: Sharing the benefits of openness to promote common prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Sharing the benefits of openness to promote common prosperity Visitors view an exhibit at the Cadillac booth at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Han Shuo) As a major engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region is characterized by deep economic integration and closely interconnected industrial sectors. Through business matchmaking and industrial cooperation, the China International Import Expo (CIIE) has provided a broad platform for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies to share opportunities and promote development, contributing to deeper and more substantive progress in building an Asia-Pacific community. The ninth CIIE, held in east China's Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10, coincided with the 2026 APEC China Year. Exhibits from APEC economies traveled far and wide to the expo, where displays, discussions, and business matchmaking turned exhibition booths into starting points for cooperation and products into bridges to new markets. U.S. exhibitors secured more than 50,000 square meters of exhibition space, the largest area among participating economies for the eighth consecutive year, up 1,500 square meters from the previous year. A robot performs a picking task at the booth of a South Korean company at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Cao Pengcheng) Canadian and New Zealand exhibitors recorded their largest exhibition areas to date, while Australian exhibitors expanded their space by 25 percent year on year. These figures reflect strong participation by APEC economies, with both exhibition scale and product diversity continuing to grow. Marriott International, which has participated in the CIIE for nine consecutive years, has witnessed the continued expansion of China's consumer services market. Mao Yibing, a member of Marriott International's global executive committee and president of the company's China operations, said China's continued efforts to promote high-standard opening-up, its thriving tourism market, and evolving consumer demand have created broad opportunities for international hotel groups. In 2021, New Zealand-based Pacific Alpacas brought more than 100 alpaca duvets to the CIIE. The products quickly sold out at its 9-square-meter booth. A year later, the company shipped 3.3 metric tonnes of New Zealand alpaca fiber to China and partnered with Chinese companies to process the material using China's advanced fiber-combing techniques. In 2025, it established long-term partnerships with Chinese e-commerce platforms. Hu Tao, chairman of Pacific Alpacas, said the CIIE provided the company with not only access to a vast market but also opportunities to work with various partners to improve its products and upgrade its industrial and value chains. A visitor learns about specialty products from a Malaysian exhibitor at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Li Anqi) For many small and medium-sized enterprises from APEC economies, the CIIE has opened up valuable opportunities to expand their markets and reach global consumers. Australian Natural Biotechnology Pty. Ltd (ANB) has participated in every edition of the expo, with its main product, Karibee Eucalyptus Pure Honey, continuing to gain popularity in the Chinese market. Alpaca wool toys from Peru have also used the CIIE as a springboard into China, with orders generated at the expo helping more than 200 local artisan families improve their livelihoods. APEC helps economies across the Asia-Pacific build consensus through dialogue and consultation and promote free trade and open cooperation, while the CIIE provides an important platform for translating these shared goals into tangible outcomes, said Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, president of the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia. The expo not only facilitates access to the Chinese market for products from participating economies, but also strengthens trade ties among APEC members, he noted. This year's CIIE focused on cutting-edge industries and innovation, showcasing new technologies, products, and services from participating economies and helping APEC economies tap into opportunities arising from China's high-quality development through innovative offerings. During the expo, many visitors tried out Singaporean company OSIM's flagship massage chair, which made its China debut at the event, at Hall 5 of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the expo. Deserine Lim, general manager of headquarters management at OSIM China, said the CIIE served as a launchpad for cutting-edge technologies from around the world to enter the Chinese market and as an important hub connecting China's innovation needs with markets across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. She added that the expo had enabled the company to create a virtuous cycle of "rooted in China, empowering the Asia-Pacific," allowing innovative products that integrate global technologies with local Chinese needs to benefit consumers across the Asia-Pacific region more effectively and quickly. The development of the Asia-Pacific region has shown that openness and cooperation create mutual benefits. This year's CIIE brought together leading companies from across regional industrial chains, fostering partnerships to strengthen the stability of regional industrial and supply chains. The Canada International Trade Promotion Society (CITPS) has brought Canadian companies to the expo for nine consecutive years. Jeannie Cheng, president of the CITPS, said the CIIE serves as a trade and economic bridge connecting businesses and markets, and that behind a product's journey into Chinese households lies a cooperation network spanning multiple APEC economies. She cited Canadian seafood and fresh fruit as examples, explaining that Canadian companies handle production and quality control, while Chinese partners are responsible for imports, distribution, and sales and economies such as Singapore and South Korea provide financial, logistics and testing services. By leveraging their respective strengths at different stages, economies across the region are strengthening economic ties and deepening cooperation, she said. Zhang Daijun, executive vice president of Samsung China, said the CIIE offers a vivid illustration of China's commitment to expanding high-standard opening-up, and that the expo is underpinned by China's vast domestic market, well-developed industrial chain support system, and vibrant innovation ecosystem. China has become a global manufacturing hub, a major center for research and development, and a key hub in global supply chains, he said. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, from November 18 to 19. Business negotiations, technology launches, and investment projects at the CIIE have offered concrete examples of Asia-Pacific cooperation. Under the summit's theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the shared vision of openness, innovation, and cooperation is being translated into practical action across the region, injecting fresh momentum into common development. item.title: Media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week opens in Shenzhen, China's Guangdong
item.description:

Also present at the event were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Addressing the event in the Great Hall of the People, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. Xi noted that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said.
